atoms.text: This guide configures MirrorSync to replicate objects from the bucket prod-orders-us-east to the bucket prod-orders-dr-us-west for disaster recovery. MirrorSync reads each new object version from the source bucket and writes an identical copy to the destination bucket within the replication window. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes. Create a role named mirrorsync-replication-role whose trust policy allows the MirrorSync service principal to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetObject, s3:GetObjectVersion, and s3:ListBucket on prod-orders-us-east, and s3:PutObject on prod-orders-dr-us-west. Do not edit the bucket policy on either bucket, because the role's policy carries all of the permissions. In the replication rule, set the role's ARN as the execution identity and apply the rule to all prefixes. Upload a test object to the source bucket and confirm that its replica appears in the destination bucket with the same ETag. If the replica status shows FAILED, check the role's policy for a missing action or a mistyped bucket name.

This guide configures MirrorSync to replicate objects from the bucket prod-orders-us-east to the bucket prod-orders-dr-us-west for disaster recovery. MirrorSync reads each new object version from the source bucket and writes an identical copy to the destination bucket within the replication window. Access is granted only through the buckets' resource-based policies, which name the MirrorSync service principal. No IAM role is created for this setup. Add a statement to the policy on prod-orders-us-east that allows the service principal to perform s3:GetObject, s3:GetObjectVersion, and s3:ListBucket. Add a statement to the policy on prod-orders-dr-us-west that allows the same principal to perform s3:PutObject. In the replication rule, set the service principal as the execution identity and apply the rule to all prefixes. Upload a test object to the source bucket and confirm that its replica appears in the destination bucket with the same ETag. If the replica status shows FAILED, check each bucket policy for a missing action or a mistyped principal.

This guide lets the service VaultCopy store nightly database export files in the bucket db-exports-archive. VaultCopy runs at 02:00 UTC, collects the compressed dump files from a staging location, and writes them under the prefix nightly/ in the bucket. It only writes new objects and never reads or deletes existing ones. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes. Create a role named vaultcopy-writer-role with a trust policy that allows the VaultCopy service principal to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows only s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:example:s3:::db-exports-archive/nightly/*. Leave the bucket policy of db-exports-archive unchanged. Enter the role's ARN in the VaultCopy job definition and start a manual run. Verify that the dump file appears under nightly/ with the expected size, and review the job log if the run reports an access denied error.

Do not create or attach any identity-based policy. Set the bucket name in the VaultCopy job definition and start a manual run. This guide sets up cross-account replication so that the service AcctShadow copies objects from the bucket finance-records in account A to the bucket finance-records-vault in a separate compliance account B. The data flow is one-way: AcctShadow reads objects and their tags from the source and writes copies, including tags, to the destination. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes. In account A, create a role named acctshadow-xaccount-role and set its trust policy to allow the AcctShadow service principal. Attach an identity-based policy that allows s3:GetObject, s3:GetObjectVersionTagging, and s3:ListBucket on finance-records, and s3:PutObject and s3:PutObjectTagging on finance-records-vault. Do not modify the bucket policy on finance-records or on finance-records-vault. Reference the role's ARN in the replication configuration of the source bucket. After saving, write a tagged test object and check that the copy in the vault bucket retains its tags. Replication lag for small objects is typically under a minute.

The data flow is one-way: AcctShadow reads objects and their tags from the source and writes copies, including tags, to the destination. Access is granted only through the buckets' resource-based policies, which name the AcctShadow service principal. No IAM role is created in either account. In account A, add a statement to the policy of finance-records that allows the principal s3:GetObject, s3:GetObjectVersionTagging, and s3:ListBucket. In account B, add a statement to the policy of finance-records-vault that allows the principal s3:PutObject and s3:PutObjectTagging. Do not attach any identity-based policy to any user or role. Reference the service principal as the execution identity in the replication configuration of the source bucket. After saving, write a tagged test object and check that the copy in the vault bucket retains its tags. Replication lag for small objects is typically under a minute.

This guide connects the on-premises file backup agent FileTether to the bucket branch-office-backups. FileTether scans a file server every hour and uploads changed files to the prefix server01/ in the bucket, using multipart upload for files larger than 100 MB. Versioning is enabled on the bucket so earlier file revisions are retained. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes. Create a role named filetether-upload-role and set its trust policy to allow the FileTether service principal. Attach an identity-based policy that allows s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload, and s3:ListMultipartUploadParts on arn:example:s3:::branch-office-backups/server01/*, plus s3:ListBucket on the bucket itself. Leave the bucket policy as it is. Provide the role's ARN in the FileTether console under Destination settings. Modify a file on the server, wait for the next scan, and confirm that a new object version appears under server01/.

This guide gives the restore service RewindOps read access to the bucket app-backups-primary so that it can rebuild a production environment from backup objects. During a restore, RewindOps lists the objects under the prefix snapshots/ and downloads the snapshot selected by the operator. It never writes to or deletes from the bucket. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes. Create a role named rewindops-restore-role and configure its trust policy to allow the RewindOps service principal. Attach an identity-based policy that allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket, restricted to the snapshots/ prefix with a condition, and s3:GetObject on arn:example:s3:::app-backups-primary/snapshots/*. The bucket policy remains unchanged. Register the role's ARN in the RewindOps restore profile. Run a test restore of the oldest snapshot and compare the restored file checksums against the values in the snapshot manifest.

This guide configures the service LockStep to copy backup objects into the bucket ransomware-safe-copies, which has Object Lock enabled in compliance mode with a 30-day retention period. LockStep reads new objects from the bucket ops-backups-live and writes copies to the locked bucket, and each copy receives the default retention automatically. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes. Create a role named lockstep-copy-role whose trust policy allows the LockStep service principal. Attach an identity-based policy that allows s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on ops-backups-live, and s3:PutObject and s3:PutObjectRetention on ransomware-safe-copies. Do not change the bucket policy on either bucket. Specify the role's ARN in the LockStep copy job. After the first run, request the retention settings of a copied object and confirm the retain-until date is 30 days ahead. Attempts to delete the copy before that date should be rejected.

This guide allows the service LogKeeper to back up application logs from the bucket web-logs-hot into the bucket web-logs-cold, where a lifecycle rule moves objects to an infrequent-access tier after 7 days. LogKeeper copies each log file under the prefix access/ once it is more than 24 hours old, and it records the copied keys in a manifest object. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes. Create a role named logkeeper-backup-role and set its trust policy to allow the LogKeeper service principal. Attach an identity-based policy that allows s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on web-logs-hot, and s3:PutObject on web-logs-cold, including the manifest key manifests/latest.json. The bucket policies must not be edited. Add the role's ARN to the LogKeeper schedule configuration. Trigger a manual run, then check that both the log copies and the manifest exist in web-logs-cold. Inspect the job output if any key is reported as skipped.

This guide configures the service MediaMirror to replicate only the prefix masters/ from the bucket studio-assets to the bucket studio-assets-replica in another region. MediaMirror copies video master files, which can exceed 50 GB, so it uses multipart upload and verifies each part with a checksum. Objects under other prefixes, such as proxies/, are intentionally not replicated. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes. Create a role named mediamirror-replication-role with a trust policy that allows the MediaMirror service principal. Attach an identity-based policy that allows s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on studio-assets, scoped to masters/, and s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload, and s3:ListMultipartUploadParts on studio-assets-replica. Leave both bucket policies unchanged. Set the role's ARN and the filter prefix masters/ in the replication rule. Upload a large test file to masters/ and confirm that the replica has an identical checksum, and that a file under proxies/ is not copied.
